entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7011"/><div sID="gen10758" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7011"/>3. Though God may leave them for a time under the "rod," or power (<reference osisRef="Ps.2.9">Psa 2:9</reference>), and oppression of the wicked for a time, as a chastisement, He will not suffer them to be tempted so as to fall into sin (<reference osisRef="1Cor.10.13">1Co 10:13</reference>). The wicked shall only prove a correcting rod to them, not a destroying sword; even this rod shall not remain ("rest") on them, lest they be tempted to despair and apostasy (<reference osisRef="Ps.73.13">Psa 73:13</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.73.14">14</reference>). God may even try His people to the uttermost: when nothing is before our eyes but pure despair, then He delivers us and gives life in death, and makes us blessed in the curse (<reference osisRef="2Cor.1.8">2Co 1:8</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Cor.1.9">9</reference>) [Luther].<div eID="gen10758" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen10759" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the lot--</hi>the possession, literally, "Canaan," spiritually, the heavenly inheritance of holiness and bliss which is appointed to the righteous. Sin's dominion shall not permanently come between the believer and his inheritance. <div eID="gen10759" type="x-p"/>

Sin's dominion shall not permanently come between the believer and his inheritance.

(Compare <reference osisRef="Ps.7.10">Psa 7:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.84.11">84:11</reference>). <div eID="gen10760" type="x-p"/>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7013"/><div sID="gen10761" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7013"/>5. Those who turn aside (under temptation) permanently show that they are hypocrites, and their lot or portion shall be with the wicked (<reference osisRef="Ps.28.3">Psa 28:3</reference>).<div eID="gen10761" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen10762" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">crooked ways--</hi>(Compare <reference osisRef="Deut.9.16">De 9:16</reference>; Mal <reference osisRef="2Cor.8.9">2:8, 9</reference>).<div eID="gen10762" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen10763" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">their--</hi>is emphatic; the "crooked ways" proceed from their own hearts. The true Israel is here distinguished from the false. Scripture everywhere opposes the Jewish delusion that mere outward descent would save (<reference osisRef="Rom.2.28">Ro 2:28</reference>, 29; <reference osisRef="2Cor.9.6">9:6</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Cor.9.7">7</reference>; <reference osisRef="Gal.6.16">Ga 6:16</reference>). The byways of sin from the way of life. <chapter eID="Ps.125"/>
